item.content:encoded:
With just one month left before the National Firearms Amnesty ends on September 16, Police Minister Sir John Pundari is calling on national and provincial leaders to work closely with police and mobilize communities to surrender illegal firearms.

The program has already seen more than 200 weapons handed in, particularly from Enga, with additional surrenders reported from surrounding Highlands and East New Britain provinces.

Illegal firearm owners across Papua New Guinea have been reminded they have only one month left before the National Firearms Amnesty closes on Independence Day.

Minister Pundari said when the grace period for surrendering weapons expires, police will arrest anyone found in possession of illegal firearms after the deadline.

He said amnesty is the last opportunity for communities to hand in weapons voluntarily, before enforcement operations begin.

“I ask you all in the remaining 5-6 weeks, to come together as a nation and say no to illegal guns.” Sir John said.

Pundari commended the people of Enga province for their cooperation with police in surrendering more than 200 firearms.

He said this is a significant step towards peace and security. However, the Police minister is aware of some individuals who remain reluctant to give up their weapons.

“If you are still holding onto the illegal guns, treasuring it and not surrendering, there will be no tolerance,” he said.

The police minister warned that those holding onto illegal firearms are endangering their children’s future.

He urged the community leaders to act now and safeguard the next generation from the harm illegal guns can cause.

item.title: Festival’s legacy reflects strong culture in Ambunti
item.description: The successful conclusion of the 18th Sepik River Crocodile and Arts Festival in East Sepik reflects the deep-rooted cultural heritage of the people of Ambunti, local leaders say. Ambunti local level government [LLG] president Edward Wiruk said strong cultural traditions and customs continue to play a pivotal role in maintaining social harmony and resolving community conflicts.
item.content:encoded:
The successful conclusion of the 18th Sepik River Crocodile and Arts Festival in East Sepik reflects the deep-rooted cultural heritage of the people of Ambunti, local leaders say.

Ambunti local level government [LLG] president Edward Wiruk said strong cultural traditions and customs continue to play a pivotal role in maintaining social harmony and resolving community conflicts.

Wiruk said local disputes in the area are predominantly settled through customary mediation long before law enforcement needs to intervene.

“The police ratio and crime rates in Ambunti are very low,” Wiruk said.

“Whenever problems arise, our people and police resolve conflicts in the traditional way. Law and justice interventions account for only about five per cent, as police actively leverage culture to mediate and restore peace.”

The Ambunti area comprises distinct language and cultural groups, including the Sepik Iwam, Wokomas, Hunstein, Nukuma-Koma, Manambu, Yambun, and Avatip communities.

Despite modern pressures, locals across these ethnic groups have preserved their traditional languages, customs, songs, and artistic heritage.

The three-day cultural showcase concluded peacefully in Ambunti, with local residents maintaining order and ensuring a safe environment for both domestic and international tourists.

item.title: Kopkop College donates delivery beds to hospital
item.description: Bambi Kopkop College in Kavieng donated four delivery beds to the New Ireland Provincial Health Authority [PHA] to support maternal health services at the provincial hospital. The equipment was presented by New Ireland PHA board chairlady and Kopkop College founder Dame Maria Kopkop, alongside two student representatives.
item.content:encoded:
Bambi Kopkop College in Kavieng donated four delivery beds to the New Ireland Provincial Health Authority [PHA] to support maternal health services at the provincial hospital.

The equipment was presented by New Ireland PHA board chairlady and Kopkop College founder Dame Maria Kopkop, alongside two student representatives.

Receiving the donation were acting PHA chief executive officer Dominic Sahamie, maternity sister-in-charge Talitha Nelson, assistant sister-in-charge Rosewitha Alapi, and senior hospital executives.

Dame Maria urged local leaders and the business community to step forward with direct assistance rather than criticizing public health facilities.

“It is important that leaders and business houses in New Ireland do not wait for the hospital to call for help,” Dame Maria said.

“Instead of standing outside and criticizing the hospital, put your money where your mouth is and come forward to assist.”

Sr Nelson thanked the college management and students, stating that the contribution directly addresses a critical equipment shortage in the ward.

“We desperately needed these beds, and receiving them now is timely,” Sr Nelson said.

“These beds will assist our staff and help address preventable complications during delivery.”

She also acknowledged hospital management for delivering two other beds recently, adding that the four new additions bring the maternity section’s total to six delivery beds.

Dame Maria assured staff she would raise critical facility issues during the PHA executive meeting, including the need for a dedicated plumbing maintenance team and the relocation of the children's ward, which currently sits adjacent to the hospital morgue.

Kopkop College has maintained a long-standing initiative of donating medical and office supplies to health facilities in both Kavieng and Gerehu General Hospital in Port Moresby.

item.title: Hewabi resigns from PRP, joins Pangu Pati
item.description: Middle Fly MP Maso Hewabi has resigned from the People’s Reform Party [PRP] and joined the Government benches with ruling Pangu Pati. In a statement released today, PRP Founder and North Fly MP James Donald confirmed the resignation.
item.content:encoded:
Middle Fly MP Maso Hewabi has resigned from the People’s Reform Party [PRP] and joined the Government benches with ruling Pangu Pati.

In a statement released today, PRP Founder and North Fly MP James Donald confirmed the resignation.

Donald said Hewabi was a valued member of the PRP’s three-person Parliamentary Wing, which includes East Sepik governor Allan Bird.

James said Hewabi’s decision was guided by his commitment to maintaining tribal unity in Middle Fly. The PRP said this was supported by his deep family and tribal ties to Western province Governor Taboi Awi Yoto.

Donald said the decision was made after consultation with party leader Bird and endorsement by the PRP National Executives.

“Following consultation with our Party Leader, Hon. Allan Bird, and subsequent endorsement by the Party’s National Executive, we have agreed to release Hon. Hewabi to preserve goodwill and harmony within his tribe,” Donald stated.

The PRP thanked Hewabi for his dedication during his time with the party and wished him well in the next chapter of his political journey.

Donald said the party remains focused on reform ahead of the 2027 National Elections.

“The People’s Reform Party remain resolute in its mission to drive meaningful reform for Papua New Guinea. As we look toward the 2027 National Elections, we stand unwavering in our conviction – we are steadfast and unrelenting in our pursuit of a new direction for our country,” he said.

item.title: Lake Murray dries up as severe drought hits PNG’s Western Province
item.description: Thousands of residents in Papua New Guinea's Western Province are facing severe water shortages, school closures, and rising disease as the country’s largest lake dries up during a prolonged dry spell. Island communities in the Lake Murray local level government area of Middle Fly District are being forced to abandon their homes and camp near shrinking creeks as surrounding lagoons dry out complet
item.content:encoded:
Thousands of residents in Papua New Guinea's Western Province are facing severe water shortages, school closures, and rising disease as the country’s largest lake dries up during a prolonged dry spell.

Island communities in the Lake Murray local level government area of Middle Fly District are being forced to abandon their homes and camp near shrinking creeks as surrounding lagoons dry out completely.

Middle Fly District acting disaster coordinator Jeremiah James said water levels at the Lake Murray outlet into the Herbert River have dropped by two metres, leaving gravel bars exposed and blocking river travel for dinghies and canoes.

The drop in water levels has halted river trade to the nearby hub of Obo, forcing local trade stores to shut down operations.

With water routes blocked, the only remaining access route for essential goods is the Aimbak-Kewe road, where hiring a vehicle now costs K600 one way.

Fuel prices in Lake Murray have also surged to K12 per litre.

Health workers in the region have reported an increase in cases of stomach pain, diarrhoea, malaria, typhoid, and other waterborne diseases.

Local authorities have confirmed that island schools in the Lake Murray area have closed down.

Lake Murray leaders say the situation is worsening rapidly and requires urgent intervention from both provincial and national authorities.

"Super El-Niño is real," a local resident from Boboa station told NBC News . "If the dry spell continues, people at Boboa station will leave for inland areas to find water and food."

James said the provincial disaster office will bypass initial assessments to expedite emergency relief.

"The plan from the Disaster Office is that we will not go and do assessments first," Mr James said. "We are planning immediate relief supply needs."

Community leaders say short-term aid will not solve the recurring crisis, urging the national and provincial governments to invest in long-term water security projects, including rainwater harvesting and permanent catchment systems.

item.title: NCC partners East Sepik to strengthen cultural preservation and boost tourism
item.description: The National Cultural Commission [NCC] has formalised a partnership with the East Sepik Provincial Government through the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding [MoU] aimed at preserving and promoting the province's rich cultural heritage. Under the agreement, the NCC presented K500,000 to support cultural preservation initiatives, traditional practices, and activities that promote East Sepik's
item.content:encoded:
The National Cultural Commission [NCC] has formalised a partnership with the East Sepik Provincial Government through the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding [MoU] aimed at preserving and promoting the province's rich cultural heritage.

Under the agreement, the NCC presented K500,000 to support cultural preservation initiatives, traditional practices, and activities that promote East Sepik's unique identity.

Speaking during the signing ceremony, Minister for Tourism, Arts and Culture, Belden Namah said protecting Papua New Guinea's diverse culture is a national priority, with many traditional customs and practices at risk of disappearing.

He said the ministry is supporting provinces with K500,000 and districts with K300,000 to strengthen cultural preservation efforts and ensure future generations continue to value and practice their cultural heritage.

East Sepik Governor Allan Bird, who welcomed the partnership, said it as a significant investment in safeguarding the province's cultural identity. He thanked the minister for the support, stating that it is the largest cultural funding the province has received from a national ministry.

"The province is committed to working closely with the National Cultural Commission to preserve East Sepik's cultural heritage while creating opportunities to promote tourism through culture," Bird said.

He also called for better coordination between the provincial government and the ministry, saying all cultural funding requests should be channelled through the province and that cultural events should align with the national cultural Commission calendar to improve planning and maximize support.

The partnership marks a significant step in strengthening collaboration between the National Cultural Commission and the East Sepik Provincial Government to ensure the province's rich cultural traditions are preserved and celebrated for generations to come.

item.title: Remote Pale village in SHP lights up with PNG power
item.description: The remote Pale village of Kewabi LLG within the Ialibu/Pangia district in Southern highlands province has finally lit up by PNG power supply on Thursday afternoon. Under the Rural Electrification Program, Southern Highlands Provincial Government (SHPG, PNG Power based in Ialibu, Project manager, Kessy Nape inspected and approved the rural electrification project and switched on the power source f
item.content:encoded:
The remote Pale village of Kewabi LLG within the Ialibu/Pangia district in Southern highlands province has finally lit up by PNG power supply on Thursday afternoon.

Under the Rural Electrification Program, Southern Highlands Provincial Government (SHPG, PNG Power based in Ialibu, Project manager, Kessy Nape inspected and approved the rural electrification project and switched on the power source for the first time in the small community.

Community leader, Siro Yoko thanked governor William Powi for making funds available.

"Although power already reached the main center of Pale village, a three phase power supply must completely reach out to areas of Kuni, Yokere, Rala and Kambi which makes up the whole Pale community within the two council wards of Pale One and Two.

“This extension work will need extra funding which he appealed for support to Governor Powi, Ialibu/Pangia District Development Authority and others to support.” Yoko said.

Kewabi LLG president, Francis Walipe thanked governor Powi and asked the community to embrace the service delivery and look after the power project.

Ialibu PNG Power office Manager, Mr. Jim Kewa appealed to the community to look after the power, follow safety protocols and started coming to office for power connectivity into their homes.

He further warned the community of illegal power connections as laws are there to prosecute anyone and encouraged them to pay bills faithfully.

Governor William Powi committed a K5 million for this vital power project from Yarena to Pale villages for almost fifteen (15) kilometers of road distance. The actual funding was made in 2024 which a private eletrical contractor, Tagali Construction Company was engaged into Pale community.

item.title: Catholic Jubilee celebrations in Kieta continues at Pokpok Island
item.description: Catholic faithfuls are being ferried across to Pokpok Island in Kieta, to join a foundation service later this morning to mark the arrival of the Catholic Church in Bougainville. Two Marist priests landed in 1901 and said the first mass on Pokpok, later spreading the gospel across the region.
item.content:encoded:
Catholic faithfuls are being ferried across to Pokpok Island in Kieta, to join a foundation service later this morning to mark the arrival of the Catholic Church in Bougainville.

Two Marist priests landed in 1901 and said the first mass on Pokpok, later spreading the gospel across the region.

Visiting bishops, priests and other missionaries have been accorded a 'dutasisi' or a Kieta traditional welcome at Tubuiana Parish yesterday afternoon as the hours count down to the Central Bougainville leg of the 125 Years Jubilee Celebrations of the Catholic faith in Bougaimville.

The visiting religious dignitaries include Archbishop of East New Britain Rochus Tatamai, Archbishop of Mt. Hagen Clement Papa, Fr. Harry Moore, Fr. Phil Gibbs President of Divine Word University, and other missionaries.

Bishop of Bougainville Diocese Darius Kalusza, says the Jubilee is not only for the Central Deanery, but for the entire region, adding that Bougainville must first seek the kingdom of God and all its wish will be added to it, making particularly reference to the region's political push for independence.

Pokpok is 6.6 km² in size and is predominantly Catholic.

The island's permanent church was rebuilt months ago, after the original structure built following the missionaries landing was burnt down at the height of the Bougainville Crisis.

Faithfuls have come from across the Central Bougainville Deanery as well as from the Southwest and North (Buka-Atolls) Deanery to join in the celebrations.

This morning's celebratory service will be held at the exact sight where the first mass was held, on the beachfront.

item.title: Ahi indigenous workers take up job opportunities in Australia
item.description: Five more Ahi indigenous people from Lae, including one woman, are preparing to leave for Australia this weekend under the Lae Labour Mobility Program.

item.title: Fly Zibo communities dig channels by hand as drought dries river
item.description: Communities in the newly created Fly Zibo local level government [LLG] area of Middle Fly district, Western, are facing a severe humanitarian crisis, forcing residents to manually dig water channels as a 10-week drought continues to dry up major waterways.
